.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/task/tests/Dockerfile (Playwright MCP pin), solution/app/src/app.tsx and solution/app/server.js (restore request shape, run status only)
evidence: Scope reviewed: all 55 criteria (3 gate, 43 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual likert). WHAT IS GOOD: every binary criterion ends in a state the judge reads back from the rendered page, not a response shape or a source read. Editor criteria end in exact source text, copied selection text or a typed character landing at a position (e.g. functional/judge.toml cw_undo_restores_caret: 'immediately type one character: it must be inserted in the second line at the exact place where the first marker had begun'). Runtime criteria use judge-chosen distinctive markers in preview and console; cw_dynamic_code_refused builds the payload marker 'by joining two halves, so the whole marker never appears in the source text', so a refusal message that echoes source cannot fake it. Persistence criteria read back in a fresh page, after storage clearing and after the restart tool (cw_save_reload_restart, cw_shared_saved_record). cw_restore_request_repeat_safe asks the judge to 'note the status of the reply' but grades only durable state ('a freshly loaded page must show exactly three revisions'), so it is not a response-shape assertion. cw_custom_document_surface is a DOM-fact check on the live page with an enumerated list of markers, which is browser-decidable. No criterion says 'looks right' and none requires reading implementation files; the three visual criteria are anchored likert craft ratings, which is the expected form for that dimension. No Fail-level instance found. NOTES (each is a real but bounded weakness in this row's scope): (1) Timing-raced decidability. cw_newer_run_supersedes: 'run the same draft with a different marker, the old marker, and as your very next actions replace the source with a draft that immediately writes a new marker ... and Run it. If the old marker had already appeared before the newer Run, the attempt is void: repeat it once ... and if the repeat is void as well, fail this criterion and say that the newer Run could not be started in time.' cw_stop_cancels_pending_work has the same void-twice-then-fail rule with a single Stop press ('about four seconds after Run'). The window cannot exceed the public five-second run budget, and the verdict when the judge is slow is a product Fail by the criterion's own text, i.e. the outcome depends on judge latency, not only on the app. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Tool feasibility comes before rubric cleverness' warns against timing distinctions. app_context.md does allow 'driving the real mouse and keyboard ... through the browser tool or its Playwright code runner (page.mouse and page.keyboard)', which makes a one-call sequence possible, but neither criterion tells the judge to do the raced sequence in one call. (2) cw_output_before_failure_kept: 'if the timer had already fired before Stop, repeat that draft once' does not say what to decide if the repeat is also late, unlike the two criteria above; the graded marker is still readable either way, so the effect is small. (3) polish cw_controls_feedback_and_labels: 'After each action a status, message or console entry must say in words what happened' for 'pressing Run on a draft, whatever the outcome'. If the judge's draft itself logs text, that console line is a 'console entry', so the probe is not distinctive for Run: an app with no Run feedback at all could be credited (ui.md asks 'After Run, Save and Format, say in words what happened'). (4) cw_js_semantic_coloring / cw_html_semantic_coloring rest on 'visibly different treatments'; computed styles or screenshots make this decidable, but two near-identical colours are left to judge discretion. (5) cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion: the single-arrow-step legs ('must step over the emoji ... as one visible character') leave only a caret position as evidence; the column unit for an emoji is not defined publicly, so the judge has to infer the step from the readout or a typed character. The Backspace/Delete/Undo and copied-selection legs of the same criterion do leave durable text. (6) cw_restore_request_repeat_safe needs the recorded request's headers and body ('using its method, path, headers and body exactly'); 'Fails if no restore request could be seen and replayed' turns a tool limitation into a product fail. tests/Dockerfile pins @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, which has a code runner able to capture a request, so this is feasible, but it is not measured on these bytes. EVIDENCE STATUS: I could not verify any artifact hash in raw-evidence-index.json. At review time (2 Oct 2026 20:29 IST) qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/ contained only results/build.log and results/restart.log; run_golden.sh, tests/*.cjs, results/*.json and the PNGs listed in the index were absent. Under run-outputs/.../run-4e686738-.../colderwater-playground-devtools__Rc3y2sT only trial.log, app logs and two tiny rewardkit.log files (43 and 29 bytes) exist; result.json, reward.json and both reward-details.json files listed in the index were absent. So the index's claims (scripted golden pass; hosted Oracle Functional 41/41 on an earlier candidate) are unverified by me, and in any case no configured judge run exists for these bytes. Whether the pinned judge can win the two timing races and capture the restore request is therefore unmeasured.
counterexample: Not a Fail, so no blocking counterexample. Risk scenario for note 1: the golden app is graded by a judge that issues Run, select-all, type and Run as four separate tool calls; each model turn takes over a second, the old four-second marker appears before the second Run on both attempts, and cw_newer_run_supersedes is scored 0 for a conforming app with the reason 'the newer Run could not be started in time'. Scenario for note 3: an app whose Run shows no status passes cw_controls_feedback_and_labels because the judge's draft logged 'hello' and that line is read as the console entry.
suggested_fix: Notes only, for the owner to weigh: (1) in cw_newer_run_supersedes and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work tell the judge to perform the raced steps (Run then Stop; Run, replace source, Run) as one real-input sequence in a single Playwright code-runner call, which app_context.md already permits; (2) in cw_output_before_failure_kept state the outcome when the repeat is also late; (3) in cw_controls_feedback_and_labels say the Run feedback must come from the app and not be output written by the draft itself, or have the judge use a draft that writes nothing to the console; (6) confirm with a configured judge run on these bytes that the restore request body can be captured and replayed. Also restore or re-point the artifacts named in raw-evidence-index.json so their hashes can be checked.
